name: Nagano (Zenkō-ji)
tagline: A temple town: Togakushi soba, oyaki and the vegetarian table of Zenkō-ji's temple lodgings.
history: Nagano grew up as the town of Zenkō-ji temple. The pilgrimage to Zenkō-ji became a popular craze in the Edo period, and temple lodgings (shukubō) sprang up to take in the pilgrims: today there are 39 (25 Tendai, 14 Jōdo), and anyone can sleep in one and dine on shōjin ryōri, Buddhist vegetarian cooking.

Nagano is soba country out of necessity: cold mountains, difficult rice, and buckwheat that likes altitude and mist. As early as the 17th century the Honchō Shokukan ranked Shinshū buckwheat above the rest, and in 1983 the prefecture declared hand-made soba a 'cultural asset of flavour'. Togakushi, a sacred mountain of ascetics north of the city, has the prefecture's most famous soba, served in little heaps on a bamboo sieve.

Oyaki is the mountain bread: rice yielded little, so people made wheat dumplings stuffed with nozawana, aubergine or beans, baked in the ashes of the irori. In central Nagano they're usually steamed; in Ogawa they still show the old way.
winter: Togakushi is under deep snow in January: check the soba houses are open. Hatsumōde (the year's first temple visit) at Zenkō-ji on 1–3 Jan is huge, with ceremonies on 1–3 Jan and the stamp on the head (御印文頂戴) from 7 to 15 Jan. Apples and new-season nozawana.

meibutsu.story: Shinshū is soba country out of necessity: cold mountains, difficult rice, and buckwheat that likes altitude and mist. As early as the 17th century the Honchō Shokukan ranked Shinshū buckwheat above the rest. Take one heap at a time, dip it, and breathe in the buckwheat.

meibutsu.name: Oyaki
meibutsu.what: A wheat dumpling stuffed with nozawana, aubergine, pumpkin or beans. Grilled on the irori or steamed.
meibutsu.where: Ogawa no Shō Daimon, on the Zenkō-ji approach.
meibutsu.glance: A wheat dumpling stuffed with nozawana greens, aubergine or beans.
meibutsu.story: Rice yielded little in these mountains, so people made their own bread: wheat dumplings stuffed with nozawana greens, aubergine, pumpkin or beans, baked in the ashes of the irori, the sunken hearth. In central Nagano they're usually steamed now, but Ogawa still shows the old way, grilling them on the irori. On the Zenkō-ji approach, try nozawana and aubergine, and eat them hot in your hand.

meibutsu.name: Shukubō shōjin ryōri
meibutsu.what: Buddhist vegetarian dinner and breakfast at a temple lodging, with tofu, mountain vegetables and sesame.
meibutsu.glance: Buddhist vegetarian dinner at a temple lodging: tofu, mountain greens, sesame.
meibutsu.story: Nagano grew up as Zenkō-ji's temple town. In the Edo period the pilgrimage became a popular craze, and temple lodgings sprang up to take in the pilgrims. Today there are 39, 25 Tendai and 14 Jōdo, and anyone can sleep in one. Dinner and breakfast are shōjin ryōri, Buddhist vegetarian cooking: tofu, mountain vegetables and sesame. Each lodging is booked directly, and it's all easy for Fernanda.
